numerical_failure.observed_behavior: predict_proba() returns NaN values for some inputs when decision_function() returns large negative values for every class; the normalization divides by a zero sum (RuntimeWarning: invalid value encountered in divide at prob /= prob.sum(axis=1)), and log_loss then raises a ValueError on non-finite input. Issue reports NaN rows for samples 18 and 374 across all 10 classes.
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: predict_proba() returns a valid categorical probability distribution over the classes; the fix assigns equal probability to each class in this case.
trigger_conditions: linear model with log loss (e.g. SGDClassifier with loss='log_loss') whose trained coefficients are large
decision_function() returns large negative values for every class for a single input
all probabilities become zero in floating point arithmetic (e.g. exp(-1000) = 0), so the normalization divides by zero
reported with SGDClassifier and default alpha during minibatch training

numerical_characteristics.magnitude: decision_function returns large negative values for every class; example exp(-1000) = 0 in floating point
category_specific_evidence: Probabilities from exp of large negative decision_function values underflow to zero in floating point, so the OvR normalization divides by zero and yields NaN/inf (example exp(-1000) = 0)
Violated property: OvR probabilities should sum to 1 after normalization; when all class probabilities are zero the row sum is zero and division produces NaN
Fix assigns uniform probabilities (prob set to 1 and prob_sum set to n_classes) for rows whose sum is zero, so each class gets 1/n_classes
Affected estimator per issue and PR: SGDClassifier with log loss, multiclass OvR setting
Issue reports NaNs from predict_proba with large model coefficients and ValueError 'Input contains NaN' downstream
Added test test_predict_proba_lr_large_values checking _predict_proba_lr handles large negative values
reproduction_risks: Exact dtype and precision of the arrays are not stated in the passages
Exact coefficient or decision_function values that trigger the failure are not given beyond exp(-1000) example
